learn: Review: hola, buenos días, buenas tardes, ¿cómo estás?, me llamo..., mucho gusto, adiós.
Use "tú" with friends and "usted" with adults you should respect.
"¿Qué tal?" is a casual "How's it going?"
lessons.try: Hold a two-minute conversation greeting a new student.

learn: Ser: soy, eres, es, somos, son.
Use ser for origin (soy de...), identity (es estudiante) and lasting traits (es alto).
"Ustedes son" is "you all are."
lessons.try: Write five sentences about your family with ser.

learn: Adjectives match nouns in gender and number: el chico alto, la chica alta, los chicos altos.
Adjectives ending in -e or a consonant change only for number: inteligente, inteligentes.
Most adjectives come after the noun.
check: At the end of the sentence
lessons.try: Describe three friends with matching adjectives.

learn: Estar also means "to be": estoy, estás, está, estamos, están.
Estar is used for location and temporary states.
"¿Dónde está el baño?" means "Where is the bathroom?"
lessons.try: Write where five things are in your house using estar.

learn: Contento (happy), triste (sad), cansado (tired), enojado (angry), nervioso (nervous), enfermo (sick).
"Estoy cansada" means "I (female) am tired."
Feelings change, so they use estar.
lessons.try: Say how you feel at five times of the day.

learn: Remember DOCTOR for ser: Description, Occupation, Characteristic, Time, Origin, Relationship.
Remember PLACE for estar: Position, Location, Action, Condition, Emotion.
"Es aburrido" (it's boring) versus "Está aburrido" (he's bored).
lessons.try: Choose ser or estar in ten sentences.

learn: Comer (to eat), beber (to drink), leer (to read), aprender (to learn), correr (to run).
Endings: -o, -es, -e, -emos, -en.
"Como" means "I eat"; "comemos" means "we eat".
lessons.try: Conjugate "leer" in all forms.

learn: Vivir (to live), escribir (to write), abrir (to open), compartir (to share).
Endings: -o, -es, -e, -imos, -en.
Only the nosotros form differs from -er verbs: vivimos.
lessons.try: Write five sentences with -ir verbs.

learn: "¿Dónde vives?" (Where do you live?) "Vivo en..."
"¿Qué lees?" (What are you reading?)
Mix -ar, -er and -ir verbs to describe a routine.
lessons.try: Interview a classmate about their weekly activities.

learn: Tener (to have) is irregular: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tienen.
"Tengo un perro" means "I have a dog."
"¿Cuántos años tienes?" asks "How old are you?"
lessons.try: Tell a partner your age and pets using tener.

learn: Spanish uses tener for many feelings: tener hambre (hungry), tener sed (thirsty), tener frío (cold), tener calor (hot), tener miedo (afraid), tener sueño (sleepy).
"Tengo frío" means "I'm cold."
"Tener razón" means "to be right."
lessons.try: Act out five tener expressions for others to guess.

learn: "Tener que" + infinitive means "to have to".
"Tengo que estudiar" means "I have to study."
Use it to talk about obligations.
lessons.try: List five things you have to do this week.

learn: Ir (to go) is irregular: voy, vas, va, vamos, van.
"Voy a la escuela" means "I go to school."
a + el contracts to "al": "Voy al parque."
lessons.try: Say where you go each day of the week.

learn: El parque, la biblioteca (library), el mercado (market), el cine (cinema), la tienda (shop), el museo.
"¿Adónde vas?" means "Where are you going?"
Combine with time: "Voy al mercado el sábado."
lessons.try: Draw a town map with Spanish labels.

learn: Ir a + infinitive talks about the near future: "Voy a comer" (I'm going to eat).
Time words: mañana (tomorrow), esta noche (tonight), el fin de semana (the weekend).
"¿Qué vas a hacer?" means "What are you going to do?"
lessons.try: Describe your plans for next weekend.

learn: In some verbs, the stem vowel changes in all forms except nosotros.
Querer (to want): quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, quieren.
Others: pensar (to think), empezar (to begin), preferir (to prefer).
lessons.try: Conjugate "pensar".

learn: Poder (to be able): puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden.
Others: dormir (to sleep), volver (to return), jugar (u → ue: juego).
"¿Puedo ir al baño?" means "May I go to the bathroom?"
lessons.try: Write sentences with dormir, poder and jugar.

learn: Pedir (to ask for): pido, pides, pide, pedimos, piden.
Others: servir (to serve), repetir (to repeat).
"Pido una pizza" means "I order a pizza."
lessons.try: Role-play a waiter and customer using pedir and servir.

learn: "¿Qué tiempo hace?" means "What's the weather like?"
Hace calor (it's hot), hace frío (cold), hace sol (sunny), hace viento (windy).
Llueve (it's raining), nieva (it's snowing), está nublado (it's cloudy).
lessons.try: Give a weather report for your town in Spanish.

learn: La primavera (spring), el verano (summer), el otoño (autumn), el invierno (winter).
Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere: December is summer in Argentina.
"En invierno hace frío" means "In winter it's cold."
lessons.try: Describe each season where you live.

learn: Most Spanish-speaking countries use Celsius: 30 grados is hot.
Link weather to activities: "Cuando hace sol, nado."
"Cuando" means "when."
lessons.try: Write five sentences linking weather and activities.

learn: La camisa (shirt), los pantalones (trousers), la falda (skirt), el vestido (dress), los zapatos (shoes), la chaqueta (jacket).
"Llevo" means "I'm wearing."
Colours follow and match: una camisa roja.
lessons.try: Describe what you are wearing today.

learn: "¿Cuánto cuesta?" (How much is it?) "Cuesta veinte euros."
"¿Qué talla usa?" asks your size.
Barato (cheap), caro (expensive).
lessons.try: Role-play buying clothes with a partner.

learn: Este/esta (this), estos/estas (these).
Ese/esa (that), esos/esas (those).
"Quiero esta camisa" means "I want this shirt."
lessons.try: Point to items and use the right demonstrative.

learn: La cocina (kitchen), el dormitorio (bedroom), el baño (bathroom), la sala (living room), el comedor (dining room), el jardín (garden).
"Mi casa tiene tres dormitorios."
Prepositions: encima de (on top of), debajo de (under), al lado de (next to).
lessons.try: Describe your home's rooms in Spanish.

learn: Hacer la cama (make the bed), lavar los platos (wash dishes), sacar la basura (take out rubbish), barrer (sweep), cocinar (cook).
"Tengo que lavar los platos" means "I have to wash the dishes."
"¿Quién hace...?" asks "Who does...?"
lessons.try: Make a chore chart for your family in Spanish.

learn: Informal commands for tú use the él/ella form: "¡Limpia tu cuarto!" (Clean your room!)
Some are irregular: haz (do), pon (put), ven (come), ten (have).
Commands are used for instructions and requests.
lessons.try: Write five commands a parent might give.

learn: Las Posadas in Mexico reenacts Mary and Joseph's search for shelter in the nine nights before Christmas.
Los Reyes Magos (Three Kings' Day) on January 6th brings gifts in Spain and Latin America.
Carnaval is celebrated with parades before Lent.
lessons.try: Research one holiday and present it in Spanish and English.

learn: A quinceañera celebrates a girl's 15th birthday in many Latin American cultures.
Families gather for meals; Sunday lunches can last hours.
"El santo" (saint's day) is celebrated in some families.
check: Family meals in many Spanish-speaking cultures are...
lessons.try: Compare a quinceañera with a coming-of-age tradition you know.

learn: Salsa (Caribbean), tango (Argentina), flamenco (Spain) and cumbia (Colombia) are famous dances.
Many celebrations include traditional dress.
Music helps you learn a language naturally.
lessons.try: Learn the words to a traditional Spanish song.
